label: Early result
confidence_note: A detector counts the closed lane itself, so the number of diverted drivers is measured, not inferred. Where they go and the delay come from simulated routes and simulated signal timings (the real phases at Faraday St, SUMO's own elsewhere), which reproduce the counts on 90% of counted street-hours.

other.label: Faraday Street eastbound (normally 41 cars an hour, reaches 28% of a lane's capacity)
Cardigan Street southbound (normally 187 cars an hour, reaches 48% of a lane's capacity)
Grattan Street westbound (normally 301 cars an hour, reaches 65% of a lane's capacity)

cars.summary: About 890 southbound drivers over the works hours must leave Swanston Street at Faraday Street. On the signed detour the fullest street, Grattan Street westbound, reaches 65% of a lane's capacity, and a diverted trip takes about 32 seconds longer.

public_transport.summary: Tram and bus services were not simulated. Bus 546 uses the closed lane. Buses 241 and 402 use Grattan Street on the signed detour, where the drive time for a car does not change.

trucks.summary: All vehicles are simulated as cars. Trucks are not modelled on their own.

assumptions: Every hour of the works (9:30am to 3:30pm on a weekday) simulated separately after a 30 minute warm-up, 5 random seeds each, and added up.

Closure: the car lane of Swanston Street southbound between Faraday Street and Grattan Street (232 m). The other direction, bikes and footpaths stay open. The plan's note banning a right turn from Grattan St into Swanston St northbound is not modelled.

Diverted drivers: cars entering the closed lane in the normal runs, 888 to 895 over the works hours. SCATS detector 5 of site 4392 counts that lane at the Melbourne University tram stop: 888 cars over the same hours (August 2026 weekday medians).

Main case: drivers drive their normal route to the closure, go round by the signed detour (Faraday Street, Cardigan Street and Grattan Street) and rejoin their route after the block. If instead every driver knows beforehand and picks their own way, most leave Swanston Street a block early and the load moves to Cardigan Street southbound and Queensberry Street westbound.

Traffic fitted to car counts per approach from SCATS stop-line detectors at 7 junctions around the site (detector roles from DTP signal sheets, some from 2008 and 2014), and to whole-site totals at 6 others, using SUMO routeSampler.

Calibration: in the normal runs the simulated traffic matches the counts within GEH 5 on 90% of counted street-hours. Mean speed 20 km/h. At most 0.3% of cars could not enter within 5 minutes and were dropped.

Street network from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors), car streets only, left-hand traffic, turn restrictions and lane arrows from OpenStreetMap. Swanston St / Faraday St runs the phases and walk times of its 2024 DTP signal sheet (site 4392): drivers turning left into Faraday St wait for the 15 s pedestrian walk, and the tram stop crossings get their own phase every cycle. Every other junction uses SUMO's delay-based actuated control, not the real SCATS plans. SCATS sets the real cycle length minute by minute and does not publish it.

Delay is the extra travel time of the same trips with and without the closure. For all traffic, two normal runs differ by up to 18 vehicle-hours over the works hours on their own, and the closure runs differ from normal by -9 to 27, so no area-wide delay is reported. For the diverted trips alone the floor is 0.4 vehicle-hours.
Street capacity is a planning value: 700 cars an hour per lane through signals.

Queue: the longest jam in an hour on Cardigan Street southbound, Faraday Street to Grattan Street, the longest of the queues on the approach and signed detour that grow by more than two normal runs differ.
Cars only. No trams, buses, trucks, cyclists or pedestrians were simulated.

findings.title: Close Faraday St westbound at Cardigan St
findings.summary: Faraday Street westbound can only turn into the closed lane at Swanston Street, so it becomes a dead end while the works are on. About 60 cars an hour arrive there.
findings.impact: Drivers reach the closure with no way out and have to turn around in Faraday St.
findings.why: About 370 cars use this approach over the works hours (SCATS detector count). The signed detour starts on Swanston Street, so nothing turns these drivers away.
findings.recommendation: Put a road closed ahead sign on Faraday St at Cardigan St, local access only, so drivers turn off before the block.
findings.source: Street network from OpenStreetMap and SCATS detector counts

findings.title: Agree a detour for bus 546
findings.summary: Bus 546 (Heidelberg to Melbourne University) drives the closed lane of Swanston Street. It needs its own detour while the works are on.
findings.impact: Buses reach the closure and take the car detour unplanned, run late, or miss stops.
findings.why: A diverted service needs the operator's agreement, and passengers need to know where it stops.
findings.recommendation: Tell the operator and the Department of Transport and Planning before the works start. Agree the detour and any temporary stop, and sign it. The route comes from OpenStreetMap, so confirm it against the current timetable first.
